summary: Feature request: per-region rollback thresholds + Dedicated-tier-specific SLOs for auto-rollback policies
description:
Requester: NexPort Analytics (Dedicated)
Contact: Platform Eng (via CSM)

Issue summary
NexPort is requesting:
1) Ability to configure rollback thresholds per region (at minimum us-east vs eu-west).
2) Dedicated-tier-specific SLO definitions for rollback decisioning (latency + error), distinct from hosted/self-serve defaults.

Background / customer context
- NexPort runs Dedicated capacity in us-east and eu-west.
- They use Redwood Console rollouts with canary traffic shifts and have started testing automated rollback using internal alerting + manual rollback.
- They report baseline latency in eu-west is consistently higher due to downstream dependencies and want less aggressive latency thresholds there.
- They also want stricter/explicit Dedicated-tier SLOs (and visibility into what SLO the system is using) because they treat rollback as a change-management control.

Impact
- Current policy configuration forces a single global threshold, leading to:
  - false positives in eu-west (rollbacks during normal variance)
  - overly conservative thresholds globally (delayed rollback in us-east when there is a real regression)
- Customer is evaluating enabling auto-rollback more broadly but is blocked on per-region policy controls.

Requested behavior
- Policy schema should allow specifying thresholds and/or evaluation windows by region.
  - Example: latency_p95_ms(us-east) <= 650ms; latency_p95_ms(eu-west) <= 900ms
  - error_rate_5xx(us-east) <= 0.30%; error_rate_5xx(eu-west) <= 0.35% (or similar)
- Dedicated-tier SLOs:
  - Ability to select “Dedicated” as the tier for rollback monitors and have the SLO computation/targets align with the dedicated contract (and exclude noisy non-customer traffic).
  - Ideally shown in Console (what SLO was evaluated + the monitor identity used).

Current behavior (as understood by Support)
- Rollback policy thresholds are effectively global at the route/model level; region scoping is not available (or not reliably wired end-to-end) for rollback decisions.
- SLO monitors/queries are not consistently separated by customer tier in a way customers can reason about in Console.

Workarounds discussed
- Create separate routes/endpoints per region (e.g., /v1/chat-us-east and /v1/chat-eu-west) and attach different policies per route.
  - Customer notes this increases application complexity and is not a long-term fit.
- Use a single conservative threshold to avoid eu-west false positives.
  - Customer notes this reduces protection against regressions in us-east.

Internal notes / roadmap link
- This request aligns with the Auto-rollback on SLO breach integration project scope: standardized monitor identities by route/model/region/tier and tiered SLO definitions.
- Tracking against Product/Rollouts roadmap item (internal): PM-482 “Auto-rollback on SLO breach integration” (monitor identity contract + policy schema).

Next steps
- Confirm current Dedicated-tier SLO definitions NexPort expects (p95/p99 latency, 5xx definition, evaluation window).
- Confirm whether NexPort needs per-region thresholds only for latency or also for error.
- Provide expected ETA once PM confirms rollout phase that includes region/tier scoping in policy schema + monitor identity.

2025-01-27 10:12 PT — Paula Mendes (Reporter)
Logged after CSM escalation. NexPort wants region-specific thresholds and explicit Dedicated tier SLO targets for rollback automation. They referenced prior false-positive rollbacks during low-traffic periods in eu-west and want more control before enabling auto-rollback broadly.

2025-01-27 11:28 PT — Rafael Mendes
SRE view: we can build monitors with region filters, but the rollout-controller auto-decision path currently doesn’t consistently select region-specific monitors (and the identity contract is in flux). Also: Dedicated vs self-serve separation is messy for a few routes; INT-3310 tracks missing labels we need for clean queries.

Recommendation: treat as roadmap dependency; offer workaround of separate routes if they must have per-region behavior now.

2025-01-27 12:10 PT — Benji Okafor
Control plane: Policy schema today doesn’t allow per-region thresholds; we store one set per route/model. Region scoping is planned in the new schema work. Monitor identity contract (route/model/region/tier) is part of the auto-rollback integration project; until then we can’t guarantee correct selection.

If customer is okay with it, we can propose a “two-policy” workaround only if they can split traffic at the route level. Otherwise it’s roadmap.

2025-01-28 09:02 PT — Paula Mendes
Customer asked whether Dedicated tier SLOs can differ from Hosted. They specifically want:
- Latency SLO target per region
- Ability to review which SLO/monitor drove a rollback decision (auditability)

I pointed them to our upcoming auto-rollback SLO integration work and asked for their desired thresholds + evaluation windows so we can bake defaults / validate against our SRE SLO definitions.

2025-01-29 15:44 PT — Allison Grant
Added internal linkage to auto-rollback SLO integration. Region + tier are explicitly in scope for the monitor identity contract and query templates.

Action requested from customer: provide (a) the endpoints/routes they care about, (b) target latency percentile and numbers per region, (c) how they want errors defined (5xx only vs includes timeouts/429), and (d) whether thresholds should compare against baseline (previous stable) or be absolute.

2025-02-03 13:21 PT — Paula Mendes
Sent NexPort the workaround options:
1) Split routes per region to apply separate thresholds (works today, higher app complexity).
2) Keep single threshold but increase min-traffic + warm-up window to reduce eu-west noise.

Also shared that we’re actively implementing region/tier-aware monitor identity + policy semantics under the auto-rollback project, and we can follow up with an ETA once the rollout plan is locked.

Status set to Waiting on Customer for threshold details + confirmation on workaround acceptability.

2025-02-04 09:55 PT — Paula Mendes
Customer replied: they do not want route-splitting long-term; they can temporarily increase warm-up/min-traffic if we can guarantee per-region controls are coming. They’ll send proposed thresholds later this week. Keeping ticket open until we receive thresholds and can map to our SLO definitions for Dedicated.
